set_text.text: Purchase price variance is the gap between what you paid for an item and its standard price, times the quantity bought. Paying more is unfavorable and paying less is favorable. It measures price alone, with quantity held still. It is how a buyer checks whether a supplier held the agreed price.
Teams differ on when they count it: when the goods arrive or when the invoice posts. Pick one point and hold it, or one month will not compare with the next.
Payment terms. A supplier can hold the $22.00 price and give you fewer days to pay. Your cost of buying rises, and no variance shows it.
Start with the lines you buy most. A 1.8% gap on a slow item is small change. The same gap on your busiest line repeats on every delivery.
Who uses a purchase price variance calculator
It is built for independent food distributors who buy against agreed supplier prices. Anyone who approves invoices or owns a cost budget should see each gap in dollars.
